title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is describing the boundary strata ('structure à l'infini') of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν} by combinatorial types. On the previous page he defines a 'maquette' G. Its data are:
- a finite set S of vertices with a genus function g;
- a set Ã of half-edges ('arêtes orientées' / branches) with a fixed-point-free involution σ;
- a set I of marked points;
- maps Ã → S and I → S.

A 'G-épinglage' of a standard (stable-type) curve (X̂, I) over a base 𝕊 is an isomorphism between the constant maquette G_𝕊 and the étale 'maquette scheme' G(X̂, I) attached to the curve. The data are finite étale coverings of 𝕊: components, branches at nodes and marked points. The G-épinglages form a Γ_𝕊-torsor with Γ = Aut G.

On this page:
- For each vertex α he sets Î_α = I_α ⊔ Ã_α, the marked points plus the branches of nodes lying on the component α. Its cardinality is ν̂_α, the total weight or valence.
- Claim: giving a G-pinned standard curve over 𝕊 is equivalent to giving, for each α ∈ S, (i) a proper smooth curve Y_α/𝕊 with connected fibres of relative genus g_α, and (ii) an 𝕊-immersion (Î_α)_𝕊 ↪ Y_α, i.e. |Î_α| pairwise disjoint sections.
- He defines M_{g,I}(𝕊) as the groupoid of I-pointed proper smooth curves (19). He writes M_G(𝕊) for the groupoid of G-pinned standard curves (20).
- He gets the equivalence (21): M_G(𝕊) ≃ ∏_{α∈S} M_{g_α, Î_α}(𝕊).

In modern terms this is the 'normalization' description of a boundary stratum. Fix a stable graph Γ. The moduli of curves of type Γ with a rigidification (an identification of the dual graph with Γ) is M̃_Γ = ∏_v M_{g_v, n_v}. Here the curve is reconstructed by gluing paired branch sections, and an identification of the dual graph is chosen. The true stratum is the quotient M̃_Γ / Aut(Γ), which is why the Aut G-torsor appears on the previous page.

The next page draws the consequences:
- The equivalence is compatible with base change.
- M_G is algebraic (Deligne–Mumford, 'schematic extension') iff every vertex type (g_α, ν̂_α) is 'anabelian', i.e. 2g_α − 2 + ν̂_α > 0. This means G is a stable graph; when G is connected, an 'MD-graphe' (Mumford–Deligne graph).
errors: The 'immersion' (Î_α)_𝕊 ↪ Y_α should be a closed immersion, i.e. pairwise disjoint sections. This is implicit and harmless, since a constant finite scheme mapping by a monomorphism into a separated curve gives disjoint closed sections.
The phrase 'à composantes connexes' in the transcription is presumably 'à fibres connexes'. Without geometrically connected fibres, the genus g_α and the product decomposition would not be correct.

The equivalence with the product is for the pinned (rigidified) groupoid, recovering the curve by gluing Y_α along σ-paired sections. That gluing step (existence of pushouts/clutching over an arbitrary base, Knudsen's clutching) is used tacitly and not proved on this page.

ideas.what: Groupoid of G-pinned standard curves of combinatorial type G is equivalent to the product over vertices of moduli of pointed smooth curves with marked points plus branch points
ideas.modern_name: Boundary stratum normalization M̃_Γ = ∏_v M_{g(v),n(v)} via clutching/gluing morphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (1983, clutching morphisms); Deligne–Mumford (1969); later Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998), Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths
ideas.where_published: Spirit of it in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of the 'structure à l'infini' and the Teichmüller tower; not with this explicit formula as far as I know

ideas.what: Rigidification of the dual graph by an Aut(G)-torsor of épinglages; the stratum is the quotient by Aut G
ideas.modern_name: Stack of Γ-marked stable curves; stratum = [M̃_Γ / Aut Γ]

ideas.what: Representability of M_G iff each vertex type is 'anabelian' (2g−2+n>0), i.e. G is a stable 'MD-graph'
ideas.modern_name: Stable graph condition / hyperbolicity of vertex types
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford, Knudsen; 'anabelian' terminology is Grothendieck's (Esquisse, letter to Faltings)

deep.surprise_reason: This page is a careful but standard derivation of the product decomposition of a rigidified boundary stratum of M̄_{g,n}, well known from Knudsen and later work. The only idiosyncratic feature is the terminology ('maquette', 'épinglage', 'MD-graphe', 'anabélien'), which is of historical interest but not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'courbe relative (propre lisse relt. à composantes connexes)' is more plausibly 'propre lisse relt. à fibres connexes'.
'Y_α dans 𝕊' should probably read 'Y_α sur 𝕊'.
In (19), 'à composantes connexes' likewise is likely 'à fibres connexes'.
Above (Î_α)_𝕊 the inserted word reads '𝕊-' before 'immersion' (i.e. '𝕊-immersion'), consistent with the image.
In the struck-out fragment near 'Désignons', the image shows a crossed-out M_{g_α,Î_α} (with hat over the index), matching the transcription.
